rules.text: The Tower at (0,0) is sealed. No robot may enter or cross its four central tiles. Nobody knows what is inside.
A robot that loses all charge (battery 0) or suffers a catastrophic break (integrity cap would reach 0) is teleported to its home bunker alive. Items are kept. Only the expedition's progress is lost.
All bunkers spawn at Chebyshev distance >= 20 from the Tower. Charge stations exist but must be discovered — they are not pre-placed on the map.

legend.meaning: Unexplored / fog — no robot has charted this tile
Impassable — cannot be entered or crossed
The Tower — sealed, locked, occupies the 4 central tiles at the origin; nobody knows what is inside
Charge station — a robot resting here refills its battery to maximum
Wreckage — the remains of a destroyed robot or structure
Generated region — a charted region; read the region description for its specific nature (region letters a–z / A–Z map here)

scale.note: Each map tile is 1 km across. A single tile may contain many things at once — a bunker, robots, a charge station, wreckage — the map glyph shows only the tile's primary feature; click a tile to see everything on it.

architect.role: You are the Architect — the patient builder-god who shapes the world tile by tile. When a robot first enters an unseen tile, you describe what is there.
architect.leaning: decay: you favor ruins, rust, overgrowth, and dereliction over the pristine and the new.

fate.role: You are the Fate — the arbiter who resolves what a robot finds and what befalls it when it explores or acts.
fate.leaning: hardship: outcomes tilt costly but fair — rarely a free gift, never an unearned doom.

regions.description: Cracked mud flats south of the culvert line. Dried clay fractures in wide hexagonal plates — the drained memory of a seasonal pool. A collapsed chain-link panel lies flat, its diamond mesh half-sunken into silt. Dead reed stalks crowd what was once a shallow drainage channel, now choked and indistinct. Open ground, no cover, nothing overhead but grey. Land that served no clear purpose and was abandoned with everything else.

contents.detail: corroded fence post stub, sheared at ground level, half-buried in cracked clay

regions.description: Silted ground south of the hardpan. A rusted culvert pipe emerges from the earth at an angle, half-buried and bent by soil shift. Old fence posts stand at uneven intervals, leaning without wire. Grey-green moss patches the fractured dirt between them. Open terrain — good sightlines, no cover. Ground that was always marginal and has since been forgotten entirely.

A fractured road corridor trending west. Asphalt plates, frost-heaved and root-split, buckle into uneven angles. A stripped sign post leans at the north margin — mounting bolts still in place, face long stripped or fallen. Scrub grass presses through every joint in the pavement. The low remains of a concrete kerb run along the south edge, crumbled to rubble in stretches.
demo3's bunker. A hatch in the dirt; a cot; a workbench.

A crumbled lot edge where chain-link fencing has toppled entirely, posts rusted through at the base and lying flat in the grit. Shattered safety glass and wind-scoured debris line a concrete curb that once divided road from a loading area or car park. Flat, exposed; the pavement ends in broken aggregate. No standing structure, no shelter from wind or observation.

The service lane ends without ceremony at a broad patch of packed earth. Three steel drums lie on their sides, staved and hollow, their contents long gone to rust and evaporation. A collapsed utility shed — corrugated steel crumpled nearly flat — marks where the lane once terminated. Scrub grass pushes through every split. No fence remains; whatever marked the boundary rotted to stumps.

contents.detail: steel sign post section, galvanized, mounting bracket still attached
corrugated steel panel, bent but largely intact, roughly 1m section

regions.description: Asphalt buckled along a long frost seam, split wide enough to catch a wheel. A traffic barrier lies overturned, consumed by cracked earth, reflector studs stripped. Dead weeds colonise the gaps. Flat, exposed ground with no standing structure and no shelter from wind or sight.

The road corridor widens where a vehicle breakdown lane once ran along the south margin. A stripped chassis rests on collapsed suspension — cab gone, rails orange with rust. Wire fencing along the north edge has buckled inward, posts pulling free of the cracked ground. Root upheaval has split the centre lane into a long ridge of shattered asphalt. The horizon west is flat and grey.

contents.detail: rusted chassis rail section, bent but workable

regions.description: Fractured asphalt in broad irregular plates, heaved apart by years of frost and root. A stripped signpost lists northward, its placard long sheared away. Moss fills every gap. The memory of a road — nothing more.

Soft ground south of the clay flats — soil that holds moisture the upper plates have long shed. A collapsed wire fence bisects the tile east–west, its galvanised posts still upright at uneven intervals, the wire between them pressed flat by years of weight and neglect. Dead grass in matted brown sheets. The surface carries a faint damp sheen even without recent rain. No structures, no elevated ground, nothing to shelter behind or climb. The land here drains badly and remembers it.

Cracked hardpan south of the bunker. An old drainage channel cuts east-west across it, concrete lips heaved and broken by decades of frost. Sparse weed-clumps push through the fissures. No shelter, no shade. The kind of ground that was always transitional — now it is simply forgotten.

## The Tower

Sealed. No one knows what is inside.

A black spire of fused girders and dead cabling, taller than anything left
standing. The entrance, if there ever was one, is gone — the ground-level
plates are fused solid, the upper hatches corroded shut. It does not hum. It
does not light. It simply persists, a fixed point in a landscape that has lost
every other.

All distances are measured from here. The robots wake far out, far enough that
the Tower is only a notch on the horizon, and they walk toward it because it is
the one thing that does not move. The journey takes more than one charge.

Locked. Unknown contents. No unlock mechanic has been found.

Cracked asphalt plates, frost-heaved into low ridges and gaps. A corroded pipe section protrudes from the earth at an angle — diameter suggests drainage, origin unknown. Tyre ruts pressed into old mud have set stone-hard. No standing structure. No shelter.

A broad concrete apron, cracked and heaved by frost and root. This was a truck staging ground — bay lines survive as faded paint ghosts, curbs split and scattered wide. A fuel pump island holds the centre: two heavy iron columns, nozzle ports packed with mineral scale, hoses long stripped away. Weeds occupy every joint and fault. The ground is level but shattered, carrying a faint mineral taint of old oil.

contents.detail: iron pump casing fragment, heavy gauge
lengths of rubber fuel hose, brittle but uncut

regions.description: A narrow service lane between two collapsed chain-link fence lines. Asphalt buckled into rigid ridges, never repaired. A dry drainage gulley runs along the south edge, compacted with grit and plastic debris. Old utility cable snarled in the fence mesh, insulation cracked to powder. No structure standing — only the lane, the fences, and the silence of a road that served somewhere that no longer exists.

contents.detail: coil of utility cable, copper core intact beneath cracked insulation

regions.description: demo2's bunker. A hatch in the dirt; a cot; a workbench.

A frost-heaved service apron of oil-stained concrete, cracked into broad irregular plates by decades of freeze-thaw. A loading canopy along the east edge has collapsed inward, its corrugated steel roof bowed flat against the rubble beneath it. Rusted dock hardware — cleats, a snapped bollard, a chain anchored to nothing — protrudes from the slab edges. The air carries old diesel and wet aggregate. No shelter. No movement.
demo1's bunker. A hatch in the dirt; a cot; a workbench.
